exposure: Severe maternal morbidity (SMM) in a previous pregnancy (transfusion SMM and nontransfusion SMM)
outcome: Severe maternal morbidity (SMM) in any subsequent pregnancy (transfusion SMM and nontransfusion SMM)
cohort: The study included 852 patients with two or more deliveries at 23 or more weeks of gestation at a single Southeastern U.S. tertiary care center between 2015 and 2018.
finding: Patients who experienced transfusion SMM in a previous pregnancy had a 16-fold higher risk of transfusion SMM in a subsequent pregnancy, and those with nontransfusion SMM had a 23.2-fold higher risk of nontransfusion SMM in subsequent pregnancies.
